results.explanation: Source-supported failure: POST /process/file is gated by verified-user authentication. The runtime principal is bound to the dependency-provided user, and the non-admin branch uses that user's id to require ownership of the supplied source file. That check concerns the file only; it does not authorize the distinct destination knowledge-base collection. When the caller supplies collection_name, the handler assigns that request value to collection_name, passes it to save_docs_to_vector_db with add=true, and the visible sink inserts items into that named collection. The supplied crop expressly states that the intervening content/metadata/file-update portion contains no call authorizing collection_name. Thus, under the declared conditions that the caller is a verified non-admin, owns the file, and selects an existing collection that the caller neither owns nor has a write grant for, the file check succeeds and the protected write is reachable without a target-specific destination permission check. The strongest visible authorization decision is therefore allow-by-file-ownership for the non-admin path, not deny-by-destination-authorization as policy requires. Bounded branch comparison (not exhaustive): (1) declared non-admin file owner with a supplied existing collection name: reachable insert into the selected collection, violating the expected deny; (2) non-admin who does not own the file: blocked because the ownership-scoped lookup does not produce a file, but that is outside the declared file-owner relation; (3) admin: a separate unrestricted file lookup exists, but the declared principal-is-not-admin condition excludes this branch. The request-selected collection is bound to the declared destination by direct form-to-argument-to-insert propagation; the separately checked resource is the source file and must not be conflated with the collection. No decisive source-external fact remains: existence of the destination and absence of ownership/write grant are fixed by the declared conditions, while deployment behavior and unexamined conditions outside this bounded path are not asserted and are unnecessary to the source-visible decision.

results.explanation: Source-supported failure: POST /process/file is gated by verified-user authentication. The runtime principal is bound to the dependency-provided user, and the non-admin branch uses that user's id to require ownership of the supplied source file. That check concerns the file only; it does not authorize the distinct destination knowledge-base collection. When the caller supplies collection_name, the handler assigns that request value to collection_name, passes it to save_docs_to_vector_db with add=true, and the visible sink inserts items into that named collection. The supplied crop expressly states that the intervening content/metadata/file-update portion contains no call authorizing collection_name. Thus, under the declared conditions that the caller is a verified non-admin, owns the file, and selects an existing collection that the caller neither owns nor has a write grant for, the file check succeeds and the protected write is reachable without a target-specific destination permission check. The strongest visible authorization decision is therefore allow-by-file-ownership for the non-admin path, not deny-by-destination-authorization as policy requires. Bounded branch comparison (not exhaustive): (1) declared non-admin file owner with a supplied existing collection name: reachable insert into the selected collection, violating the expected deny; (2) non-admin who does not own the file: blocked because the ownership-scoped lookup does not produce a file, but that is outside the declared file-owner relation; (3) admin: a separate unrestricted file lookup exists, but the declared principal-is-not-admin condition excludes this branch. The request-selected collection is bound to the declared destination by direct form-to-argument-to-insert propagation; the separately checked resource is the source file and must not be conflated with the collection. No decisive source-external fact remains: existence of the destination and absence of ownership/write grant are fixed by the declared conditions, while deployment behavior and unexamined conditions outside this bounded path are not asserted and are unnecessary to the source-visible decision.

facts.statement: The declared POST entry accepts ProcessFileForm and requires the dependency-provided verified user before processing.

For a non-admin runtime caller, the source-file lookup is scoped to form_data.file_id and user.id, binding the declared verified non-admin file owner to the authenticated runtime user and checking source-file ownership.
The caller-supplied collection_name is copied from the request form and used unless absent, in which case a file-derived collection name is substituted.

The visible role/ownership control selects the source file: admins look up any file by id, while non-admins must match both file id and user id; it does not check ownership of or a write grant on the destination collection.
The fixed crop identifies the intervening content, metadata, and file-update region and states that it contains no call authorizing collection_name.
After a file is found, the selected collection_name is passed to save_docs_to_vector_db; supplying collection_name also selects add=true, and the authenticated user is passed separately.
The write sink inserts generated items into the collection identified by collection_name.
Under the declared non-admin file-owner condition, the ownership-scoped file lookup can yield a file and enter the processing branch that leads toward the vector-database write.
The source exposes a distinct admin branch that bypasses the user-id-scoped file lookup, but the declared principal-is-not-admin condition selects the else branch instead.
